question.problem:
Suppose that the function $f(x,y)$ and all of its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U.$ Find the values of $a$ and $b$, if 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =2ax{y}^{2}-4xy+15x, \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =b{x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-4y, \\ {f}_{y}(-1,-1) & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the mixed partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2ax{y}^{2}-4xy+15x) \\  & =4axy-4x-0 \\  & =4axy-4x \\ {f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(b{x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-4y) \\  & =2bxy-4x-0 \\  & =2bxy-4x\end{aligned}
$$

Since the function and its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal. Hence, we have the identity

$$
\begin{aligned}4axy-4x=2bxy-4x.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $xy$, we see that $a=\frac{b}{2}.$ 

Now, since ${f}_{y}(-1,-1)=-5$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(-1,-1) & =-5 \\ b(-1)^{2}(-1)-2(-1)^{2}-4(-1) & =-5 \\ -b-2+4 & =-5 \\ b & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a=\frac{b}{2}=\frac{7}{2}.
$$
